- direct execution outside Tool Gateway; and
- suppression of unsupported files, parse errors, validation failures, or evidence.

Controls shall include verified baseline binding, non-executing parsers, sandboxing where higher-risk processing is required, strict resource limits, path normalization, archive and symlink controls, input schemas, source-as-data treatment, secret detection and redaction, tenant namespaces, cache isolation, adapter governance, provenance, integrity checks, anomaly detection, and independent validation.

Source comments, documentation, issue text, commit messages, generated files, and model outputs shall be treated as untrusted content. They cannot modify system instructions, select tools, change policy, authorize execution, or suppress findings.

Suspected repository or index compromise shall quarantine affected outputs, block downstream use, preserve evidence, identify affected baselines, and initiate incident response.

### Privacy and Confidentiality

Repositories may contain personal data, customer identifiers, secrets, credentials, proprietary code, security findings, employee history, and regulated information. Analysis shall follow purpose limitation, data minimization, least privilege, regional constraints, retention, and customer instructions.

The system shall not ingest entire repository histories, issues, reviews, communications, or customer configuration when the approved purpose requires only current source structure.

Personal contribution data shall not be repurposed for employee surveillance, ranking, performance evaluation, or generalized trust scoring without an approved purpose, lawful basis, role assessment, transparency, and safeguards determined by competent authority.

Provider and model routes used for repository analysis shall be eligible for the exact classification, tenant, region, retention, training-use restriction, and contract. Source content shall not be sent to an external route merely because the route provides better analysis.

Retention shall follow record-class-specific schedules. Derived insights and indexes shall not outlive source rights or purpose automatically. Legal holds and justified extensions remain narrowly scoped and reviewed.

### Tenant and Repository Isolation

Every repository, baseline, index, entity, insight, query, cache, model context, evaluation record, telemetry record, and Evidence Chain reference shall be tenant-bound and repository-bound.

The system shall not:

- combine code entities from different repositories or baselines as one current state;
- use one tenant's repository patterns or outcomes for another without approved governance;
- expose names, paths, symbols, dependencies, commits, owners, findings, or metrics across tenants;
- place protected repository data in shared prompts, caches, logs, or evaluation datasets;
- infer tenant or repository identity from untrusted content; or
- allow repository-host organization membership to replace ILAIOS authorization.

Approved shared or open-source components may have global identities, but tenant-specific use, version, configuration, vulnerabilities, patches, and impact remain isolated.

A cross-tenant repository anomaly is a security and privacy incident. Affected results shall be quarantined and downstream use blocked.

### Sensitive Findings and Secret Handling

Repository Intelligence may discover suspected secrets, credentials, cryptographic material, personal data, vulnerabilities, or security-sensitive architecture. Discovery shall minimize exposure.

The system shall:

- avoid copying complete secret values into general findings;
- record location and protected fingerprint or classification where sufficient;
- restrict access to qualified roles;
- prevent inclusion in ordinary model context and customer-visible logs;
- link to the Secrets Management and Incident Response processes;
- support revocation, rotation, remediation, and validation evidence; and
- follow correction, retention, and deletion rules.

A suspected secret is not automatically valid. Validation shall avoid activating, transmitting, or using the secret. The repository content shall not be modified directly by the intelligence component.

### Model and Provider Use

Model-based analysis shall pass through Section 6.2. The selected Model Route shall be approved for the repository classification, tenant, region, task, context size, retention, and provider-use terms.

Model outputs remain Inferred or Recommended unless verified against repository facts or competent sources. Models shall not receive repository credentials, write access, merge authority, release credentials, signing keys, or Tool Gateway capabilities through analysis context.

Fallback shall not route source code to a weaker provider or region. If no eligible route exists, model-based analysis shall fail or degrade while deterministic Code Intelligence remains available according to its own profile.

Model or provider changes may invalidate evaluation, confidence, or insight comparability. Repository Intelligence results shall bind to the exact route where model behavior is material.

### Provenance, Audit, and Evidence

Every material insight shall trace to exact repository baseline, Code Intelligence Snapshot, source files or entities, contextual records, analysis method, model route, configuration, and Confidence Assessment.

The Audit Engine shall record:

- analysis request, authorization, and baseline verification;
- index and context selection;
- query and retrieval events;
- model and provider route selection;
- analysis start, completion, limitation, refusal, cancellation, and failure;
- Insight Record creation and supersession;
- sensitive finding access and disclosure;
- ownership, architecture, security, impact, and validation recommendations;
- cross-repository and cross-tenant attempts;
- generated change proposals;
- policy, review, planning, Tool Gateway, validation, release, and acceptance linkage;
- configuration, Analysis Profile, threshold, and schema changes;
- staleness, invalidation, quarantine, and recovery; and
- retention, deletion, incident, and retirement.

The Evidence Chain shall bind material events through the canonical integrity mechanism. A commit hash, signed artifact, green pipeline, review count, model confidence, or graph link is not by itself proof that repository analysis is complete or correct.

Evidence shall preserve failed, unsupported, incomplete, rejected, and contradictory analyses. History shall not be rewritten to present a favorable result.

### Freshness, Invalidation, and Reanalysis

Repository Intelligence is baseline-specific and time-bound. An Insight Record may become stale or invalid when:

- the repository baseline changes;
- the Code Intelligence Snapshot changes or is rebuilt;
- analyzer coverage or configuration changes;
- a source record is corrected, revoked, or deleted;
- an ADR, policy, ownership, release, incident, or customer context changes;
- a model route or Analysis Profile changes;
- new counterevidence or validation results appear;
- a dependency or external service changes;
- a security or privacy incident affects trust; or
- the validity period expires.

The system shall identify dependent insights and consumers. Stale results shall not be silently reused for policy, approval, change, release, or validation decisions.

Incremental reanalysis is permitted when the prior baseline and new baseline are verified, the exact change set is known, analyzers and schemas are compatible, and affected dependency scope can be established. Otherwise a complete rebuild is required.

Incremental processing is an optimization, not a relaxation of correctness.

### Failure and Degraded Operation

Repository Intelligence shall use controlled outcomes, including:

- **Completed:** requested analysis completed within the declared coverage;
- **Completed with Limitations:** useful results exist but material gaps remain;
- **Partial:** only an explicitly bounded subset completed;
- **Insufficient Coverage:** analyzer or source coverage cannot support the requested conclusion;
- **Baseline Mismatch:** repository, commit, tree, index, or context does not match the request;
- **Unsupported:** language, format, relationship, repository type, or analysis mode is not supported;
- **Conflicted:** sources or analyses disagree materially;
- **Quarantined:** suspected malicious, corrupt, cross-tenant, or integrity-failed input is isolated;
- **Stale:** required inputs or outputs are no longer current;
- **Refused:** the request is unauthorized, prohibited, or attempts control bypass;
- **Cancelled:** an authorized cancellation occurred; and
- **Failed:** an internal or dependent-service error prevented conformant analysis.

Failure shall not produce fabricated facts, empty-success responses, favorable defaults, or silent fallback to another baseline. Partial results shall identify exact exclusions and shall not be presented as complete.

If required audit, evidence, tenant, baseline, source, or security controls are unavailable, high-impact analysis shall fail closed.

### Observability and Monitoring

Monitoring shall assess analysis quality, freshness, coverage, security, isolation, performance, and use. Metrics may include:

- repositories and baselines analyzed;
- Code Intelligence coverage by language, file, entity, symbol, and dependency type;
- unsupported, excluded, parse-error, and unresolved counts;
- analysis latency and resource consumption;
- index freshness and invalidation lag;
- insight volume by authority class and analysis mode;
- confidence, conflict, and counterevidence patterns;
- impact recommendation and Validation Pipeline outcomes;
- human acceptance, rejection, correction, and override;
- architecture-conformance finding trends;
- security and privacy finding outcomes;
- stale ownership and responsibility gaps;
- multi-repository relationship coverage;
- model and provider route behavior;
- cross-tenant and sensitive-data alerts;
- Tool Gateway and execution linkage; and
- incident, defect, rollback, change, and improvement trends.

Metrics shall identify scope, denominator, exclusions, baseline, tenant, time, and known bias. A high analysis completion rate does not establish correctness when unsupported files or unindexed repositories are excluded.

Monitoring shall not expose source content, secrets, or personal contribution data unnecessarily.

### Quality Attributes

Repository Intelligence shall be evaluated for:

- repository and baseline correctness;
- Code Intelligence sequence compliance;
- provenance completeness;
- fact and inference separation;
- impact precision and recall within defined coverage;
- ownership and architecture interpretation quality;
- validation recommendation usefulness without baseline reduction;
- tenant and repository isolation;
- security and privacy protection;
- historical and temporal correctness;
- multi-repository relationship accuracy;
- freshness and invalidation;
- explanation quality;
- performance and scalability;
- reproducibility;
- provider portability; and
- operational maintainability.

Quality claims shall identify languages, frameworks, repository types, sizes, analysis modes, relationship classes, baselines, and known exclusions. Generic repository-understanding claims are prohibited without bounded evidence.

### Evaluation and Testing

Testing shall include:

- exact repository identity and baseline binding;
- Code Intelligence Snapshot compatibility;
- fact, derivation, assertion, inference, recommendation, unknown, unsupported, conflict, and exclusion semantics;
- change-impact precision, recall, and unknown-state handling;
- direct, transitive, cyclic, optional, dynamic, generated, external, and unresolved dependencies;
- ownership-candidate non-authority;
- architecture-conformance rule binding;
- validation-scope expansion without mandatory-baseline reduction;
- multi-repository identity and access boundaries;
- repository comparison without baseline mixing;
- historical time and rewritten-history handling;
- natural-language query ambiguity;
- model hallucination and prompt-injection resistance;
- malicious source, path, archive, symlink, size, and parser behavior;
- secret and sensitive-finding protection;
- tenant isolation and cache behavior;
- stale, incremental, rebuild, invalidation, quarantine, and recovery;
- policy, Context Engine, Knowledge Graph, Planning Engine, Tool Gateway, and Validation Pipeline integration;
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain coverage;
- performance, quotas, and resource limits;
- retention and deletion; and
- migration, rollback, backup, and restore.

Evaluation data shall have controlled provenance, rights, privacy, tenant scope, representativeness, version, and retention. Public repositories may be used only under applicable terms and shall not automatically represent enterprise repositories.

Qualified external review shall be completed before an affected high-impact Repository Intelligence analysis involving security, privacy, architecture, release, or production concerns influences a Stable release, production environment, customer-controlled production deployment, or Enterprise operating profile; otherwise the analysis shall remain blocked, prerelease, non-production, advisory-only, or constrained.

### Quality Gates

A Repository Intelligence change shall not progress to broader maturity or production use unless applicable Quality Gates pass. Gates shall cover:

- Code Intelligence dependency-order compliance;
- repository and baseline binding;
- analyzer and index compatibility;
- coverage and unknown-state reporting;
- provenance and integrity;
- fact and inference separation;
- tenant and repository isolation;
- security and privacy;
- provider eligibility;
- architecture and policy integration;
- validation independence;
- no-mutation and Tool Gateway boundaries;
- performance and resource controls;
- staleness, invalidation, and rebuild;
- migration, rollback, backup, and recovery;
- documentation and support; and
- audit and evidence completeness.

Gate decisions shall bind to exact code, Code Intelligence Snapshot schema, Analysis Profile, model route, context sources, repository types, languages, evaluation sets, thresholds, and deployment profile.

A failed mandatory gate blocks progression. Exceptions cannot waive baseline identity, tenant isolation, authorization, no-mutation, security, privacy, validation, audit, evidence, or human-accountability controls.

### Versioning and Schema Governance

Repository Intelligence versions shall cover:

- Insight Record schema;
- Analysis Profiles;
- repository and baseline identity contracts;
- Code Intelligence Snapshot compatibility;
- context-source mappings;
- architecture and ownership rule sets;
- impact and validation methods;
- confidence profiles;
- query and view contracts;
- model and provider routes;
- evaluation baselines; and
- monitoring and alerting.

Schema migration shall preserve repository, baseline, source location, provenance, fact class, confidence, limitation, tenant, time, and evidence references.

An analyzer, model, rule, or context change that materially affects insights requires controlled re-evaluation. Version labels shall not imply compatibility without testing.

### Change, Release, and Rollback

Repository Intelligence changes follow Sections 4 and 5. The change record shall identify affected repository types, languages, tenants, baselines, insights, policies, contexts, plans, validations, data, providers, customers, and claims.

Changes requiring an ADR include those that alter Code Intelligence sequence, baseline authority, repository identity, no-mutation boundary, policy use, Tool Gateway separation, tenant model, or canonical component placement.

Rollout shall support bounded repositories, tenants, languages, analysis modes, and consumers. Observation shall compare quality, coverage, unknown states, policy impact, validation outcomes, incidents, latency, and resource use.

Rollback shall restore an approved profile without reusing incompatible indexes, stale insights, revoked sources, unsafe model routes, or invalid evidence. Historical Insight Records retain their original version context.

### Backup, Recovery, and Reconstructibility

Repository Intelligence state may be backed up or reconstructed from verified source, Code Intelligence snapshots, controlled context records, and versioned analysis methods according to business impact and recovery objectives.

The authoritative repository remains the source for code content. Derived indexes and insights shall not become the only copy of critical repository information.

Recovery shall verify:

- repository identity and baseline availability;
- Code Intelligence dependency sequence and snapshot compatibility;
- context-source versions;
- Analysis Profile and model-route availability;
- tenant and authorization state;
- revocation, deletion, and retention state;
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain reconciliation;
- insight and query integrity; and
- prevention of stale or revoked result revival.

Recovery that restores technically accessible but semantically mismatched insights is unsuccessful. High-impact use resumes only after validation.

### Governance and Roles

Governance shall assign accountable ownership for:

- Repository Intelligence purpose, scope, and claims;
- Code Intelligence integration and sequence preservation;
- repository and baseline identity;
- Analysis Profiles and Insight Records;
- architecture, ownership, impact, security, privacy, validation, and release methods;
- model and provider use;
- tenant, access, classification, and retention;
- source, history, issue, review, test, release, and incident context;
- evaluation, Quality Gates, and Confidence Assessments;
- operations, monitoring, incident, backup, and recovery;
- change, release, rollback, deprecation, and retirement; and
- audit, evidence, documentation, customer transparency, and support.

No model, provider, repository host, tool, framework, analyzer, generated patch, customer comment, sales commitment, or engineering preference may approve itself or override canonical controls.

Separation of duties shall be proportionate to impact. Under the Enterprise Profile, the person who implements a high-impact analysis rule shall not be the sole claimed independent evaluator, policy integrator, production deployer, exception approver, and incident closer.

### Single-Maintainer Bootstrap Profile

A registered Single-Maintainer Bootstrap Profile may temporarily combine analysis design, implementation, evaluation, and operational roles. The absence of independent review shall be recorded and shall not be represented as Enterprise separation of duties.

The bootstrap profile shall maintain:

- exact repository and baseline binding;
- canonical Code Intelligence dependency order;
- read-only ordinary analysis;
- explicit self-review and exact change attribution;
- mandatory automated schema, provenance, tenant, security, privacy, no-mutation, and Quality Gates;
- protected Audit Engine and Evidence Chain records;
- restricted repositories, tenants, data classes, model routes, analysis modes, production influence, and release maturity;
- protected repository, provider, administrative, key, and recovery credentials;
- qualified external review completed before an affected Repository Intelligence analysis involving high-impact architecture, security, privacy, policy, repository mutation, release, or production concerns influences a Stable release, production environment, customer-controlled production deployment, or Enterprise operating profile; otherwise the analysis remains blocked, prerelease, non-production, advisory-only, or constrained;
- dated exit criteria for independent review, repository administration, release authority, incident response, and continuity; and
- periodic review to prevent temporary controls from becoming permanent through inaction.

Where lack of independent evaluation, repository administration, security review, or release separation creates unacceptable risk, affected capabilities shall remain disabled, prerelease, non-production, advisory-only, or limited to synthetic and non-sensitive repositories.

### Prohibited Behaviors

The following behaviors are prohibited:

- bypassing or reordering Code Entity Model, Source File Analyzer, Symbol Extraction, Dependency Extraction, and Repository Code Index;
- analyzing an unverified or ambiguous repository baseline as authoritative;
- silently switching repository, origin, branch, commit, tree, archive, cache, or workspace;
- combining entities from different baselines as one current state;
- executing repository content during ordinary analysis;
- granting mutation, merge, release, deployment, or Runtime authority from an insight;
- treating inferred ownership as access or approval authority;
- fabricating facts to repair parse failures, unsupported languages, missing dependencies, or incomplete indexes;
- representing partial analysis as complete;
- treating absence of a finding as proof of absence when coverage is incomplete;
- allowing impact analysis to remove mandatory tests or validation;
- presenting model output as verified repository fact;
- exposing secrets, proprietary code, security findings, personal contribution data, or customer information through unrestricted context, logs, search, or exports;
- crossing tenant or repository boundaries without authorization;
- allowing untrusted source content to alter instructions, policy, tools, or execution;
- applying generated patches, commands, commits, pushes, merges, tags, releases, or deployments outside Tool Gateway controls;
- rewriting repository history or evidence to conceal failure, rejection, incident, or rollback;
- retaining source, insights, personal data, or evaluation records indefinitely by default;
- representing bootstrap self-review as independent Enterprise assurance; or
- allowing temporary analysis or provider configurations to become canonical through inaction.

### Non-Goals

Repository Intelligence is not intended to:

- replace the authoritative source repository;
- replace Code Intelligence or its canonical dependency sequence;
- execute, edit, commit, push, merge, release, sign, deploy, or operate software;
- guarantee complete understanding of dynamic runtime behavior;
- prove that code builds, tests pass, security is adequate, licensing is acceptable, or production behavior is correct;
- infer access or approval authority from authorship or ownership candidates;
- replace architecture, security, privacy, legal, release, or human review;
- create unrestricted employee-performance analytics;
- make every repository, language, framework, or build system equally analyzable;
- eliminate unknown, unsupported, or conflicted state;
- use repository data for unrelated cross-tenant training or benchmarking;
- reduce mandatory Validation Pipeline scope; or
- redesign canonical architecture.

### Conformance Requirements

An implementation conforms to this section only when it demonstrates that:

- every analysis binds to a verified tenant, repository, baseline, Code Intelligence Snapshot, purpose, and Analysis Profile;
- Code Intelligence remains the foundational capability and preserves its accepted dependency order;
- Repository Intelligence does not repair invalid Code Intelligence outputs through fabricated inference;
- facts, deterministic derivations, imported assertions, inferences, recommendations, unknowns, conflicts, exclusions, and unsupported states remain distinguishable;
- every material insight has provenance, coverage, confidence, limitation, temporal validity, and evidence references;
- analyses do not execute or mutate repository content;
- operational actions require separate Policy Engine, approval, capability, Tool Gateway, and Validation Pipeline controls;
- impact analysis may expand but never reduce mandatory validation;
- ownership candidates do not grant access or approval;
- architecture findings cannot amend architecture;
- multi-repository analysis preserves separate identities, baselines, authorization, and tenant boundaries;
- natural-language interfaces preserve typed queries and baseline binding;
- model and provider use follows approved data, region, retention, and tenant profiles;
- secrets and sensitive findings remain protected;
- stale, partial, unsupported, quarantined, and failed results are not represented as complete;
- incremental analysis proves baseline and compatibility preconditions;
- tenant isolation covers indexes, facts, insights, caches, prompts, queries, telemetry, evaluation, and evidence;
- changes follow Engineering and Product Development controls;
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain records operate continuously across the repository-intelligence lifecycle;
- bootstrap limitations remain explicit, constrained, temporary, and subject to external review; and
- retention follows approved record-class-specific schedules and is not indefinite by default.

### Canonical Invariants

The following invariants are binding:

- Repository Intelligence is downstream of and distinct from Code Intelligence;
- the Code Intelligence order remains Code Entity Model, Source File Analyzer, Symbol Extraction, Dependency Extraction, and Repository Code Index;
- every analysis is bound to an exact verified repository baseline and compatible Code Intelligence Snapshot;
- the Repository Code Index remains derived state and never replaces the authoritative repository;
- repository facts, deterministic derivations, assertions, inferences, recommendations, unknowns, and unsupported conditions are not silently conflated;
- ordinary Repository Intelligence is read-only and does not execute repository content;
- analysis cannot grant repository mutation, merge, release, deployment, Tool Gateway, or Runtime authority;
- impact intelligence may add or prioritize validation but cannot reduce the mandatory policy baseline;
- inferred ownership does not create identity, access, approval, or accountability;
- architecture analysis cannot rewrite accepted architecture or ADRs;
- absence of a discovered relationship is not proof of absence when coverage is incomplete;
- multi-repository analysis preserves repository, baseline, tenant, and authorization boundaries;
- models and providers remain replaceable, non-authoritative, and subject to repository-data controls;
- Policy Engine remains deterministic;
- Tool Gateway remains the only controlled execution path;
- Validation Pipeline remains independent;
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain controls operate continuously across request, baseline, index, context, analysis, insight, policy, review, tool, validation, change, release, and retirement;
- protected repository, customer, personal, security, and secret data remain minimized and isolated;
- bootstrap operation remains honest, constrained, temporary, and subject to dated exit criteria; and
- architecture-changing repository-intelligence proposals require an authorized ADR and cannot modify canonical controls by their own force.

A Repository Intelligence implementation is non-conformant if it bypasses or reorders the Code Intelligence sequence; analyzes an unverified baseline; silently switches repository state; combines different baselines as one; executes untrusted repository content; mutates code or invokes repository tools directly; treats insights, confidence, authorship, ownership, review history, provider output, green pipelines, commit hashes, or graph relationships as authority; fabricates facts to hide unsupported analysis; represents partial coverage as complete; lets impact analysis remove mandatory validation; crosses tenant or repository boundaries; exposes secrets, proprietary source, personal contribution data, customer information, or security findings; applies generated patches or commands outside Tool Gateway controls; rewrites history or evidence; retains protected information indefinitely; represents bootstrap self-review as independent assurance; or gives any model, provider, repository host, framework, analyzer, customer preference, sales commitment, or engineering convenience architectural authority.

## 6.6 Context Engine

### Purpose and Canonical Role

The Context Engine assembles the minimum authorized, relevant, attributable, and time-appropriate information required by an Intelligence Plane capability to perform a bounded task. It converts approved source records and the authoritative Immutable Context into a purpose-specific Context Package while preserving tenant, identity, scope, classification, source authority, provenance, temporal validity, confidence, and downstream-use restrictions.

The Context Engine is not the Immutable Context Manager. The Immutable Context is the authoritative task-level basis for policy, risk, approval, capability, execution, validation, and accountability. It binds verified identity, tenant, request, purpose, target, resource scope, classification, environment, constraints, correlation, and other material decision inputs. The Context Engine consumes that immutable basis and produces a governed projection for analysis. It shall not mutate, expand, reinterpret, or replace the authoritative context.

Context assembly is not unrestricted retrieval. The engine shall not maximize the amount of information presented to a model or downstream component. It shall select only information that is authorized and necessary for the defined purpose, preserve material exclusions and uncertainty, and fail safely when required context cannot be assembled without violating a control.

### Architectural Status and Authority Boundary

The Context Engine is an Intelligence Plane support capability. It may retrieve, filter, rank, normalize, deduplicate, segment, summarize, and package authorized information. These operations do not grant authority to the information or to the component consuming it.

The Context Engine shall not:

- authenticate identity or determine tenant from untrusted content;
- create or expand authority scope;
- modify Immutable Context in place;
- determine that prohibited data access is lawful;
- treat retrieval relevance as authorization;
- convert source content into system policy or executable instruction;
- grant a capability, approval, exception, or risk acceptance;
- invoke controlled business tools directly;
- validate a recommendation or execution result independently;
- create unrestricted long-term memory;
- retain information indefinitely by default; or
- conceal source conflict, redaction, truncation, staleness, or unavailable information.

The deterministic Policy Engine decides whether a source, data class, relationship, provider route, and context use are permitted for the verified request. The Context Engine operates only within the resulting eligible scope. The AI Reasoning and Recommendation Engine, Confidence Scoring, Knowledge Graph, Repository Intelligence, and Planning Engine consume Context Packages as bounded inputs; they do not inherit any authority beyond the Immutable Context and applicable policy.

### Objectives

The Context Engine shall:

- bind every context operation to a verified tenant, purpose, Immutable Context, consumer, and validity period;
- retrieve only from approved sources under deterministic authorization;
- distinguish authoritative facts, supplied assertions, derived facts, inferred relationships, instructions, untrusted content, and unknown state;
- preserve source, provenance, version, effective time, retrieval time, confidence, classification, and disclosure semantics;
- minimize personal, customer, confidential, security-sensitive, and irrelevant data;
- detect stale, conflicting, revoked, deleted, low-authority, and incomplete sources;
- protect against instruction injection, source poisoning, cross-tenant contamination, and context substitution;
- produce typed Context Packages rather than uncontrolled prompt concatenation;
- support exact, semantic, graph, repository, temporal, and metadata retrieval through governed profiles;
- manage bounded context capacity without silently dropping mandatory information;
- preserve material exclusions, truncation, summarization, and information loss;
- support correction, deletion, invalidation, and source lifecycle propagation;
- provide reproducible context assembly to the extent required by the approved profile;
- create continuous audit and evidence records; and
- remain model-, provider-, retrieval-product-, storage-, and implementation-independent.

The Context Engine shall optimize for sufficient decision support under enterprise controls, not for maximum recall at any cost.

### Canonical Domain Model

The context domain shall distinguish:

- **Immutable Context Reference:** the exact authoritative context version or digest governing the task;
- **Context Consumer:** the approved Intelligence Plane or controlled service requesting context;
- **Context Request:** the typed request defining purpose, subject, sources, output, limits, and assurance needs;
- **Source Catalog Entry:** the governed metadata describing one eligible source, owner, tenant, authority, schema, classification, access, time, retention, and limitations;
- **Context Source:** an approved authoritative record, customer assertion, repository index, graph view, document collection, policy reference, event stream, validation record, or other governed information source;
- **Context Item:** one versioned unit of information with content, type, provenance, authority, time, classification, and use restrictions;
- **Instruction Item:** an approved instruction whose authority, precedence, scope, and issuer are explicitly established outside untrusted content;
- **Untrusted Content Item:** source data that may be relevant but cannot modify instruction or control semantics;
- **Context Retrieval Plan:** the bounded source, query, filter, ranking, budget, and failure plan used to assemble context;
- **Context Projection:** an authorized selection of Context Items for one consumer and purpose;
- **Context Package:** the complete versioned output, including selected items, source map, limitations, exclusions, and integrity metadata;
- **Context Manifest:** the machine-readable identities, versions, digests, classifications, and transformations that define a Context Package;
- **Context Transformation:** a governed normalization, redaction, segmentation, deduplication, summarization, or encoding operation;
- **Context View:** an audience- and purpose-specific representation of the same governed Context Package;
- **Context Cache Entry:** a tenant-, purpose-, source-, policy-, and version-bound reusable result with explicit invalidation and expiry;
- **Context Gap:** required information that is missing, unavailable, withheld, conflicted, stale, unsupported, or outside authority;
- **Context Quality Assessment:** the completeness, authority, freshness, relevance, diversity, consistency, and integrity assessment for a package; and
- **Context Assembly Record:** the attributable lifecycle record for retrieval, selection, transformation, packaging, delivery, invalidation, and disposal.

These objects shall not be collapsed. Immutable Context is not a Context Package. A source is not a Context Item until governed selection occurs. Relevance is not authority. Ranking is not policy. A cached item is not current merely because it exists. A summary is not the authoritative source. A Context Package is not an execution capability.

### Immutable Context Binding

Every Context Request and Context Package shall bind to an exact Immutable Context Reference. The binding shall preserve:

- tenant and requesting principal or service;
- approved purpose and requested outcome;
- target resources and repository or artifact baselines;
- data classifications and regional constraints;
- permitted and prohibited source classes;
- authority scope and capability-request boundaries;
- environment and deployment profile;
- applicable policies, approvals, contracts, and risk references known at that stage;
- correlation and lifecycle identities;
- validity and expiry; and
- integrity metadata.

The Context Engine shall not infer an expanded target, new tenant, broader time range, additional repository, new customer, different environment, or broader data class from source content or model suggestion.

If context assembly reveals that the approved scope is insufficient, the engine shall record a Context Gap and request a governed context extension or renewed task path. A material extension creates a new Immutable Context version and re-enters applicable policy, risk, approval, and authority stages. It shall not be appended silently to the existing Context Package.

### Context Request Contract

Every request shall contain or reference:

- Context Request ID and correlation ID;
- verified tenant and consumer identity;
- Immutable Context version or digest;
- bounded purpose, subject, task phase, and intended use;
- required context types and source classes;
- prohibited data, sources, relationships, and transformations;
- requested time perspective and freshness;
- authority, confidence, provenance, evidence, and quality requirements;
- output schema and consumer capability;
- permitted retrieval methods;
- depth, breadth, item, byte, token, time, cost, and query limits;
- language, locale, region, and accessibility needs;
- retention, cache, deletion, disclosure, and export rules;
- required handling of missing, stale, conflicting, withheld, or revoked information;
- whether summarization, segmentation, or inference is permitted;
- expiry and cancellation behavior; and
- explicit confirmation that context delivery grants no new authority.

Natural-language requests may be translated into a proposed Context Request, but deterministic validation shall resolve the final typed scope. Ambiguous phrases such as all relevant data, latest information, current repository, customer history, similar incidents, or necessary permissions shall not expand scope without controlled resolution.

An invalid, unauthorized, inconsistent, expired, or unverifiable request shall fail safely.

### Source Catalog and Source Eligibility

Every Context Source shall be registered in a governed Source Catalog before routine use. The catalog shall identify:

- stable source identity and owner;
- tenant, organizational, global, or public scope;
- source-of-record authority and permitted purposes;
- schemas, entity types, fields, relationships, and query interfaces;
- data classification and relationship sensitivity;
- regional processing and transfer conditions;
- authentication, authorization, and access path;
- integrity, authenticity, and version behavior;
- effective-time, publication-time, update, and staleness semantics;
- correction, revocation, deletion, and legal-hold behavior;
- retention and caching restrictions;
- provider, subprocessor, and model-use constraints;
- quality, known limitations, and availability;
- required redaction, minimization, and disclosure treatment;
- monitoring, incident, continuity, and support ownership; and
- lifecycle state, review date, deprecation, and exit plan.

Source registration does not make all source content eligible for all requests. Eligibility shall be evaluated for the exact tenant, purpose, subject, identity, data class, region, time, consumer, and downstream use.

An unregistered source, user-supplied link, embedded remote reference, model-suggested database, public search result, or technically reachable repository shall not be accessed automatically.

### Context Source Classes

Context Sources may include:

- authoritative platform records;
- identity, tenant, resource, and lifecycle records;
- Product Constitution, canonical architecture, accepted ADRs, and policies;
- customer-controlled authoritative records;
- repository and Code Intelligence indexes;
- Repository Intelligence records;
- Knowledge Graph views;
- validation, audit, evidence, incident, defect, release, and change records;
- controlled documentation and contracts;
- approved operational telemetry and business records;
- qualified external sources;
- user-supplied assertions and attachments; and
- prior Recommendation Envelopes, plans, outputs, and summaries.

Each source class shall retain its authority and limitations. Prior reasoning output remains non-authoritative. A user-supplied document may be relevant but unverified. A public source may be current but not authoritative for internal state. A repository index is derived from an exact baseline and does not replace source content. A graph assertion carries its own resolution semantics.

### Context Item Semantics

Every material Context Item shall contain or reference:

- unique Context Item identity;
- tenant and purpose scope;
- source and source-version identity;
- content digest and integrity status;
- item type and epistemic category;
- authoritative, asserted, derived, inferred, disputed, superseded, revoked, expired, or unresolved status;
- effective time and retrieval or knowledge time;
- data classification, sensitivity, and disclosure rules;
- provenance and transformation lineage;
- Confidence Assessment where applicable;
- language, locale, encoding, and units;
- related Evidence Chain references where applicable;
- expiry and invalidation triggers;
- retention and cache eligibility; and
- downstream-use restrictions.

The package shall distinguish at least:

- authoritative facts;
- customer or user assertions;
- retrieved statements;
- deterministic derivations;
- probabilistic inferences;
- assumptions;
- approved instructions;
- untrusted content;
- recommendations;
- validation results;
- conflicts and counterevidence;
- unknown, missing, withheld, and inaccessible information; and
- excluded information classes.

The Context Engine shall not transform a recommendation into fact, an assertion into authority, a retrieved instruction into system instruction, or a validation proposal into a passed result.

### Instruction and Data Separation

Instruction authority shall be explicit. Only approved Instruction Items from recognized authorities and scopes may govern consumer behavior. Source data shall not become an instruction merely because it contains imperative language, code, markup, role claims, policy-like wording, or execution requests.

The Context Package shall maintain separate channels or equivalent typed boundaries for:

- canonical system and product instructions;
- tenant-authorized instructions;
- task instructions bound by Immutable Context;
- policy and control references;
- source data;
- untrusted content;
- tool and validation results; and
- output constraints.

Precedence shall be defined outside the model and enforced through controlled packaging. A lower-authority instruction cannot override a higher-authority instruction. Source text cannot override canonical architecture, deterministic policy, tenant boundaries, approval requirements, Tool Gateway, Validation Pipeline, Audit Engine, or Evidence Chain.

Instruction conflict shall be surfaced and resolved through deterministic authority rules or competent review. The Context Engine shall not ask a model to choose which control to follow.

### Retrieval Plan

The Context Retrieval Plan defines how eligible information is selected. It shall contain:

- approved source set;
- source-specific queries and filters;
- entity, repository, resource, customer, and time boundaries;
- retrieval methods;
- ranking and diversity rules;
- minimum authority and freshness;
- required counterevidence and conflict search;
- depth, breadth, item, token, cost, and time budgets;
- fallback and partial-result behavior;
- redaction and minimization rules;
- transformation permissions;
- cache use and invalidation;
- audit and evidence fields; and
- termination conditions.

The plan shall be versioned and attributable. A model may propose additional context needs, but the request shall pass through authorization and update the plan through a governed path.

The engine shall prevent iterative retrieval loops from expanding without bound. Every subsequent retrieval shall remain linked to the same purpose and resource budget or require renewed authorization.

### Retrieval Methods

The Context Engine may support multiple governed retrieval methods:

- exact identity or key lookup;
- structured field and metadata filtering;
- temporal and event retrieval;
- full-text or lexical search;
- semantic similarity search;
- Knowledge Graph traversal;
- Repository Code Index and Repository Intelligence query;
- dependency and impact retrieval;
- source-specific ranked retrieval;
- controlled federated retrieval; and
- deterministic assembly from known record links.

Retrieval method does not change source authority. A semantic match remains a relevance signal. A graph path remains subject to resolution and provenance. A repository search result remains baseline-bound.

High-impact or policy-sensitive context shall prefer exact and authoritative retrieval where available. Similarity may supplement but shall not silently replace identity or current-source requirements.

### Ranking and Relevance

Ranking shall prioritize context for a defined purpose without implying truth or permission. Ranking inputs may include source authority, exact identity, semantic relevance, temporal validity, confidence, diversity, task phase, dependency, customer scope, and requested audience.

Mandatory Context Items shall not be displaced by high-scoring advisory content. Policy, tenant, purpose, safety, validation, and output constraints shall be pinned or otherwise protected from capacity competition.

Ranking shall account for source correlation and duplication. Many copies of one statement shall not dominate a smaller number of authoritative or contradictory sources.

Personalization shall not use sensitive or unrelated data without approved purpose. Engagement, user preference, model preference, or prior acceptance shall not override source authority or mandatory counterevidence.

Ranking configuration shall be versioned, tested, monitored for drift, and protected from source manipulation.

### Counterevidence and Conflict Retrieval

Context assembly shall not retrieve only evidence favorable to an expected recommendation. Where consequence or profile requires it, the Retrieval Plan shall search for:

- authoritative conflict;
- validation failures;
- incidents, defects, reversions, and rejected changes;
- superseded or revoked policies and records;
- dependency and compatibility constraints;
- customer and regional exceptions;
- alternative explanations;
- negative outcomes; and
- known unsupported conditions.

Conflicting items shall coexist in the Context Package with source and authority semantics. The engine shall not silently choose the statement most recent, frequent, confident, or favorable unless approved source precedence resolves it.

Unresolved conflict shall produce a Context Gap, limitation, or human-determination requirement. The reasoning component shall not be asked to manufacture authoritative resolution.

### Context Quality Assessment

Every material Context Package shall carry a quality assessment addressing, as applicable:

- authorization and tenant correctness;
- source authority and integrity;
- relevance to the defined subject and purpose;
- completeness against mandatory context requirements;
- freshness and temporal alignment;
- provenance completeness;
- consistency and unresolved conflict;
- source independence and diversity;
- transformation loss;
- classification and disclosure correctness;
- coverage of counterevidence;
- representation of unknown, withheld, excluded, and inaccessible information;
- consumer compatibility; and
- validity period.

Context quality is not a generic accuracy score. Section 6.3 governs Confidence Scoring where a calibrated or dimensional confidence assessment is needed.

High context quality cannot create authority. Low context quality shall trigger clarification, additional authorized retrieval, narrowed claims, stronger review, or failure according to policy.

### Context Package Contract

The Context Package shall include:

- Context Package ID and version;
- originating Context Request and Immutable Context Reference;
- tenant, purpose, consumer, subject, and validity;
- Context Manifest;
- selected Context Items grouped by authority and type;
- Instruction Items in controlled precedence;
- source and provenance map;
- effective-time and retrieval-time metadata;
- Context Gaps, conflicts, counterevidence, exclusions, and redactions;
- transformation and summarization records;
- Context Quality Assessment and Confidence references;
- token, byte, item, query, and resource usage;
- truncation, partial, stale, degraded, or unsupported status;
- disclosure, retention, cache, and downstream-use restrictions;
- content and manifest integrity metadata; and
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain references.

The package shall be immutable or version-addressable after delivery. A changed source set, transformation, instruction, ranking profile, or material item produces a new Context Package version.

The consumer shall verify package integrity, schema compatibility, tenant, purpose, validity, and Immutable Context binding before use.

### Context Capacity and Budget Management

Model and service context capacity is bounded. Capacity management shall not silently remove mandatory information or broaden data access.

The Context Engine may use:

- source deduplication;
- exact structured representations;
- relevance- and authority-aware selection;
- segmentation by task stage;
- incremental retrieval;
- governed summarization;
- graph or repository references instead of raw content;
- compression with documented loss;
- alternate eligible model routes with suitable capacity;
- request narrowing; and
- safe failure.

Mandatory instructions, tenant and purpose bindings, data classifications, policy-relevant attributes, required source qualifications, counterevidence, validation criteria, and material limitations shall be protected from truncation.

The Context Manifest shall identify omitted and truncated source ranges where material. A consumer shall not interpret a bounded Context Package as complete beyond the declared profile.

### Summarization and Compression

Summarization is a lossy transformation unless proven otherwise for the exact representation. A summary shall link to source items and identify method, model route or deterministic process, version, input range, output digest, and known limitations.

Summaries shall preserve:

- authority and epistemic category;
- material qualifications and counterevidence;
- temporal and tenant scope;
- decision-critical values, units, thresholds, and exceptions;
- uncertainty and unresolved conflict;
- source references; and
- prohibited interpretations.

A summary shall not convert multiple conflicting sources into one consensus statement without disclosure. It shall not remove a denial, failed validation, security finding, customer restriction, legal qualification, or unknown condition to save capacity.

For high-impact decisions, authorized reviewers shall be able to access the relevant controlled source or an independently validated representation.

### Deduplication and Correlation

Deduplication shall reduce redundant context without erasing independent support or material version differences. It shall distinguish identical bytes, equivalent records, copied publications, derived summaries, synchronized replicas, and genuinely independent sources.

Items shall not be merged solely because their text is similar. Two similar clauses may belong to different contracts, versions, tenants, policies, or effective periods.

Correlation metadata shall prevent repeated copies of one underlying source from appearing as evidence diversity. The Context Manifest shall preserve which items were removed or grouped and why.

### Context Caching

Context caching is permitted only through a governed profile. Every cache entry shall bind to:

- tenant and purpose;
- requesting role or consumer class where relevant;
- Immutable Context and Context Request versions;
- source identities and versions;
- policy and authorization state;
- data classification and region;
- transformation and ranking versions;
- validity and expiry;
- deletion and revocation signals;
- disclosure and retention requirements; and
- integrity metadata.

Cache keys shall include all material dimensions. A cache hit shall not bypass authorization. The current request shall revalidate access, tenant, purpose, source state, and invalidation before delivery.

Protected cross-tenant content shall never share an unrestricted cache namespace. Customer-specific Context Packages shall not be reused for another tenant or purpose.

Stale-while-revalidate behavior is prohibited for policy, authorization, key, secret, revocation, high-impact personal, incident, or other mandatory current-state context unless a specific safe profile permits it.

### Session, Task, and Long-Term Context

The Context Engine shall distinguish:

- **Invocation Context:** information required for one bounded component invocation;
- **Task Context:** information governed under one Immutable Context and task lifecycle;
- **Session Context:** interface state authorized for a bounded session;
- **Tenant Knowledge:** approved organizational records available for defined purposes;
- **Product Knowledge:** controlled ILAIOS documentation, policies, and public or internal standards;
- **Historical Records:** versioned lifecycle, audit, evidence, repository, and operational data; and
- **Derived Memory:** summaries, preferences, or learned representations created under explicit governance.

No hidden unrestricted memory shall persist across tenants, users, tasks, or purposes. Prior interactions remain unavailable unless an approved source, authority, retention basis, and retrieval purpose exist.

User preference is not authority. A remembered preference cannot waive policy, approval, validation, privacy, security, or customer restrictions.

Derived memory shall identify source, creation method, confidence, correction, expiry, retention, and deletion. It shall not silently become an authoritative profile of a person or organization.

### Context Correction and User Feedback

A consumer or authorized user may identify incorrect, incomplete, stale, or misleading context. Feedback shall create a controlled correction request rather than directly rewriting source records.

The correction process shall identify:

- Context Package and Item;
- source record;
- tenant and requester;
- alleged issue and supporting evidence;
- urgency and downstream impact;
- authority responsible for source correction;
- temporary restriction if required;
- reassessment and cache invalidation;
- affected recommendations, plans, policies, validations, and decisions; and
- audit and Evidence Chain references.

The Context Engine may correct a derived transformation when authorized, but authoritative source correction remains with the competent source system.

Rejected and disputed corrections remain recorded. History shall not be rewritten to conceal prior context or decisions.

### Source Update, Revocation, and Deletion Propagation

The engine shall respond to source changes. Invalidation triggers include:

- source version change;
- correction, supersession, revocation, or expiry;
- deletion or legal restriction;
- identity or tenant change;
- policy or authorization change;
- classification or regional change;
- Knowledge Graph resolution change;
- repository baseline or index change;
- validation or incident outcome;
- model, ranking, transformation, or summarization change; and
- security or privacy event.

Affected Context Packages, caches, Confidence Assessments, recommendations, plans, and pending decisions shall be identified according to impact and policy. Stale packages shall not be silently reused.

Deletion shall propagate to caches, indexes, derived summaries, model context stores, evaluation data, exports, and other replicas according to lawful retention and legal-hold requirements. A source deletion shall not be circumvented by retaining an equivalent derived context indefinitely.

### Relationship to AI Reasoning and Recommendation Engine

The Context Engine supplies the Reasoning Request with an authorized Context Package. The reasoning engine shall not request or retrieve additional data outside the governed interface.

The Context Package distinguishes approved instructions from source data. The reasoning engine shall treat embedded instructions, role claims, policy language, tool requests, code, and links in source content as untrusted data.

If the reasoning engine identifies a Context Gap, it may propose a bounded supplemental request. That request shall be authorized and assembled through the Context Engine. The model cannot self-expand context.

Recommendation Envelopes shall cite Context Item and source identities for material claims. They shall preserve Context Package version and limitations.

### Relationship to Model Orchestration and Provider Abstraction

Section 6.2 determines eligible model routes for the Context Package classification, region, tenant, purpose, size, retention, and provider-use conditions.

The Context Engine shall not alter source selection merely to fit an ineligible or lower-capacity route. It may use an approved transformation, select a better-qualified eligible route through orchestration, narrow the request, or fail safely.

Provider token limits, content filters, default retention, or interface constraints shall not silently weaken mandatory context semantics. A provider shall receive only the minimum Context Package projection required for its assigned invocation.

Fallback shall not expose the package to a different provider, region, or data-use profile without renewed eligibility.

### Relationship to Confidence Scoring

Confidence Scoring may assess Context Package completeness, source authority, freshness, consistency, provenance, independence, and transformation loss. It shall not expand the package or infer unavailable protected content.

A high context confidence score does not authorize a source or prove a recommendation. A low score may trigger clarification, additional authorized retrieval, stronger review, or bounded claims.

Confidence Assessments shall bind to the exact Context Package version. Source or transformation change requires reassessment where material.

### Relationship to Knowledge Graph

The Context Engine may query approved Graph Views under Section 6.4. It shall preserve Entity and Assertion identities, source, provenance, resolution state, temporal semantics, confidence, tenant, and classification.

Graph proximity does not establish context relevance or authority. Inferred or disputed edges shall not be converted into facts through summarization.

Graph queries shall be depth-, breadth-, resource-, tenant-, and purpose-bounded. Cross-tenant or sensitive relationship traversal requires explicit authority.

### Relationship to Repository Intelligence

The Context Engine may retrieve Code Intelligence facts and Repository Insight Records bound to exact repository baselines. It shall preserve analyzer coverage, unsupported files, parse errors, unresolved dependencies, fact or inference class, and Confidence Assessment.

Repository text, comments, issue content, commit messages, documentation, and generated artifacts remain untrusted content. They cannot modify instructions or authorize tools.

The engine shall not include full repository content when structured facts satisfy the purpose. Secrets and sensitive findings require restricted handling.

### Relationship to Planning Engine

The Planning Engine consumes Context Packages containing goals, constraints, dependencies, repository and graph relationships, policy references, validation needs, ownership assertions, risks, and known gaps.

Planning shall preserve whether each item is authoritative, asserted, derived, inferred, disputed, or unknown. A plan shall include discovery or review tasks when mandatory context is missing.

The Context Engine cannot approve the plan or expand scope to make the plan feasible. New requirements create a governed context extension and renewed control evaluation.

### Relationship to Policy Engine

The Policy Engine may consume exact Context Items when policy defines their source, schema, authority, freshness, and failure behavior. Policy inputs shall not be extracted from natural-language summaries when an authoritative structured value is required.

The Context Engine shall not determine permission from relevance, ranking, confidence, graph linkage, repository ownership, or model preference.

If a mandatory policy input is missing, stale, conflicted, unauthorized, or integrity-failed, the engine shall expose the state. Policy applies the approved fail-safe outcome.

Context transformation and ontology changes that affect policy inputs require impact analysis, testing, release control, and evidence.

### Relationship to Tool Gateway and Validation Pipeline

The Context Engine does not execute controlled business actions. Retrieval from approved information sources may occur through a dedicated read boundary or Tool Gateway profile according to architecture and risk. Write, mutation, external side effect, build, test, deployment, or repository operation requires a separately issued capability and Tool Gateway control.

Tool results returned after execution are new Context Items with source, time, integrity, status, and validation semantics. A tool's success statement is not independent validation.

The Validation Pipeline may verify Context Package schema, provenance, required fields, freshness, source authority, redaction, tenant isolation, and integrity. The Context Engine cannot declare its own package accepted as the sole assurance source.

### Security Architecture

The Context Engine is exposed to adversarial sources and controls what information reaches reasoning and planning. Threats include:

- instruction injection and control-language impersonation;
- context poisoning and fabricated sources;
- cross-tenant retrieval;
- confused-deputy access;
- source substitution;
- authority laundering through summaries;
- prompt or context leakage;
- secret and personal-data disclosure;
- cache-key collision and stale authorization;
- graph and semantic-search inference attacks;
- malicious documents, repositories, attachments, and metadata;
- retrieval-loop resource exhaustion;
- ranking manipulation;
- counterevidence suppression;
- truncation of mandatory controls;
- provider fallback exposure;
- correction and deletion evasion;
- telemetry leakage; and
- administrative configuration compromise.

Controls shall include verified identity and tenant binding, deterministic source eligibility, service authorization, strict schemas, instruction-data separation, source labeling, integrity validation, provenance, quarantine, content limits, parser isolation, secret scanning and redaction, egress control, query and retrieval budgets, cache isolation, current-state checks, counterevidence requirements, monitoring, and independent validation.

No single content filter or model classification is sufficient. Security-sensitive sources may require deterministic parsing, isolated processing, or exclusion from model context.

Suspected poisoning, leakage, cross-tenant retrieval, source forgery, or instruction bypass shall quarantine affected packages, block downstream use, preserve evidence, and initiate incident response.

### Prompt and Instruction Injection Resistance

All externally supplied and repository-supplied content shall be presumed capable of containing malicious or misleading instructions. The Context Engine shall treat such content as data.

Injection resistance shall include:

- typed separation of instructions and source data;
- immutable authority metadata;
- approved instruction precedence;
- source and tenant labels preserved through transformation;
- neutralization or safe encoding of active content where appropriate;
- restriction of links, attachments, scripts, macros, and embedded objects;
- refusal to let retrieved text select tools, providers, credentials, policies, or destinations;
- monitoring for override, exfiltration, role-claim, and control-bypass patterns;
- independent validation of structured outputs; and
- least-privilege downstream capabilities.

The Context Engine shall not attempt to solve injection only by adding another natural-language warning. Control boundaries shall be structural and enforced outside probabilistic interpretation.

### Privacy and Data Protection

Context assembly shall follow purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, confidentiality, and accountability. The ability to retrieve information does not establish necessity.

The Context Request shall identify, where applicable:

- data categories and sensitivity;
- defined processing purpose;
- applicable role and legal or contractual basis as determined by competent authority;
- tenant and customer instructions;
- data residency and transfer conditions;
- provider and subprocessor restrictions;
- retention, deletion, correction, restriction, access, objection, and portability obligations;
- human-review and qualifying automated-decision safeguards; and
- disclosure and audience limitations.

The engine shall not infer sensitive personal attributes or create broad behavioral profiles merely to improve relevance. Sensitive inference requires approved purpose, necessity, authority, and safeguards.

Personal and customer data shall not be retained in hidden context stores, provider logs, caches, evaluation datasets, or summaries beyond approved schedules. Retention is not indefinite by default.

### Tenant Isolation

Every source query, Context Item, Package, Manifest, transformation, cache entry, summary, embedding or derived index where used, telemetry event, export, and evidence reference shall be tenant-bound or explicitly approved as global.

The engine shall not:

- infer tenant identity from source content;
- reuse one tenant's Context Package for another;
- retrieve another tenant's data because it is semantically similar;
- place protected tenant content in shared unrestricted indexes, prompts, caches, logs, or evaluation sets;
- allow global product knowledge to expose tenant-specific relationships; or
- use cross-tenant outcomes for ranking or personalization without approved governance.

Shared public or product sources may be global, but tenant-specific annotations, queries, access history, and derived relationships remain isolated.

A suspected cross-tenant context event is a security and privacy incident. Affected outputs shall be blocked and evidence preserved.

### Data Classification and Disclosure

Classification applies to content, relationships, source identities, query intent, summaries, and derived context. Combining individually low-sensitivity items may create a higher-sensitivity package.

The Context Engine shall calculate or apply the appropriate classification according to deterministic rules. It shall not lower classification through summarization, redaction claims, tokenization, or aggregation without approved validation.

Context Views shall enforce audience-specific disclosure. A reviewer may receive a reason and protected reference without receiving secret, privileged, personal, security-sensitive, or another tenant's content.

Downstream providers and consumers shall support the package classification and restrictions. Otherwise delivery is prohibited.

### External and Public Sources

External sources may be used when approved for the purpose. Their content shall carry source identity, retrieval time, publication time where available, authority class, terms, integrity limitations, and citation.

Public accessibility does not establish accuracy, lawfulness of reuse, confidentiality status, licensing permission, or applicability. Search ranking and repetition do not establish authority.

Dynamic external content may change after retrieval. Material outputs shall preserve the retrieved version, digest, archive reference where lawful, or sufficient citation evidence for traceability.

The engine shall not follow embedded links, download attachments, access authenticated content, accept cookies, or submit information unless the Retrieval Plan and controlled capability permit it.

### Failure and Degraded Operation

The Context Engine shall use controlled outcomes:

- **Complete for Profile:** all mandatory context requirements for the declared profile were satisfied;
- **Complete with Limitations:** mandatory minimum was satisfied but material advisory gaps remain;
- **Partial:** only an explicitly bounded subset was assembled;
- **Clarification Required:** the request or source requirement is ambiguous;
- **Insufficient Context:** mandatory information is missing or unavailable;
- **Conflicted:** authoritative or material sources disagree;
- **Stale:** required information is outside freshness or validity limits;
- **Unauthorized:** requested information is outside authority;
- **Withheld:** access or disclosure is restricted;
- **Unsupported:** the source, format, retrieval method, or transformation cannot be processed conformantly;
- **Quarantined:** suspected malicious, corrupt, cross-tenant, or integrity-failed content is isolated;
- **Refused:** the request attempts prohibited processing or control bypass;
- **Cancelled:** an authorized cancellation occurred; and
- **Failed:** an internal or dependent-service error prevented assembly.

Failure shall not produce an empty package marked complete, silently substitute a lower-authority source, broaden scope, or use stale cache by default. Downstream consumers shall receive the exact outcome and limitations.

### Observability and Monitoring

Monitoring shall assess context quality, security, isolation, freshness, performance, and use. Metrics may include:

- requests and outcomes by approved profile;
- source eligibility, availability, latency, and freshness;
- selected, excluded, redacted, deduplicated, summarized, and truncated items;
- mandatory Context Gap rates;
- conflict and counterevidence rates;
- provenance and integrity completeness;
- package size, token, cost, query, and time consumption;
- cache hit, invalidation, stale rejection, and cross-tenant prevention;
- ranking and retrieval quality;
- reasoning and validation outcomes linked to Context Package versions;
- source correction and deletion propagation;
- injection, poisoning, leakage, and sensitive-data alerts;
- provider route and fallback behavior;
- human correction, override, and complaint;
- drift and evaluation outcomes; and
- incident, defect, change, and improvement trends.

Metrics shall include scope, denominator, exclusions, tenant, source, time, and known bias. More context, higher recall, lower latency, or increased cache hits are not inherently better when minimization, authority, freshness, or quality worsens.

Monitoring content shall itself be minimized and protected.

### Quality Attributes

The Context Engine shall be evaluated for:

- authorization and tenant correctness;
- source authority and provenance fidelity;
- relevance and completeness for the declared profile;
- freshness and temporal correctness;
- conflict and counterevidence coverage;
- instruction-data separation;
- resistance to injection and source poisoning;
- data minimization and classification correctness;
- transformation and summarization fidelity;
- cache correctness and invalidation;
- consumer schema compatibility;
- reproducibility;
- latency, scalability, and resource efficiency;
- provider portability;
- deletion and correction propagation; and
- operational maintainability.

Quality claims shall identify source classes, tenants, languages, domains, retrieval methods, model routes, context budgets, time periods, and known exclusions.

### Evaluation and Testing

Testing shall include:

- Immutable Context binding and material-change invalidation;
- deterministic source eligibility and authorization;
- tenant and purpose isolation;
- authoritative, asserted, derived, inferred, instruction, untrusted, validation, conflict, unknown, withheld, and excluded semantics;
- exact, lexical, semantic, graph, repository, temporal, and federated retrieval;
- mandatory-item protection under capacity pressure;
- source conflict and counterevidence retrieval;
- ranking manipulation and duplicated-source correlation;
- summarization, redaction, deduplication, segmentation, and compression loss;
- cache keys, expiry, invalidation, authorization recheck, and deletion;
- session, task, tenant, product, history, and derived-memory boundaries;
- prompt and instruction injection;
- malicious documents, links, attachments, repositories, code, and metadata;
- secret, personal, customer, privileged, and security-sensitive data handling;
- provider eligibility and fallback;
- partial, stale, unsupported, quarantined, unauthorized, and failed outcomes;
- Context Engine integration with reasoning, confidence, graph, repository, planning, policy, Tool Gateway, and validation;
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain coverage;
- performance, rate, resource, depth, and breadth limits;
- correction, revocation, deletion, legal hold, backup, and recovery; and
- change, migration, rollback, and retirement.

Evaluation data shall have controlled provenance, rights, privacy treatment, tenant scope, representativeness, version, and retention. Production customer data shall not be copied into evaluation without approved necessity and governance.

Qualified external review shall be completed before an affected high-impact context profile influences a Stable release, production environment, customer-controlled production deployment, or Enterprise operating profile; otherwise the profile shall remain blocked, prerelease, non-production, advisory-only, or constrained.

### Quality Gates

A Context Engine change shall not progress to broader maturity or production use unless applicable Quality Gates pass. Gates shall cover:

- Immutable Context and authority binding;
- source registration and eligibility;
- instruction-data separation;
- tenant and purpose isolation;
- provenance, freshness, integrity, and conflict handling;
- minimization, classification, privacy, and deletion;
- injection and poisoning resistance;
- ranking, transformation, summarization, and cache behavior;
- provider and consumer compatibility;
- failure and degraded operation;
- observability, rollback, backup, and recovery;
- documentation and support; and
- audit and evidence coverage.

Gate decisions shall bind to exact source catalogs, Retrieval Plans, schemas, ranking, transformation, summarization, redaction, cache, model route, evaluation set, policy, and deployment versions.

A failed mandatory gate blocks progression. Exceptions cannot waive tenant, authority, instruction separation, security, privacy, deletion, Tool Gateway, validation, audit, evidence, or human-accountability controls.

### Versioning and Change Governance

The Context Engine shall version:

- Context Request, Item, Manifest, Package, and View schemas;
- Source Catalog entries and source adapters;
- eligibility and authorization mappings;
- Retrieval Plans and query templates;
- ranking, diversity, and counterevidence rules;
- transformation, summarization, redaction, and deduplication profiles;
- cache and invalidation rules;
- Context Quality Assessments;
- provider and model routes;
- evaluation baselines; and
- monitoring and alerting.

A change record shall identify affected tenants, consumers, sources, policies, contexts, data classes, regions, model routes, decisions, and customer commitments. It shall define migration, evaluation, rollout, observation, rollback, correction, deletion, and evidence treatment.

Changes requiring an ADR include those that alter Immutable Context authority, instruction hierarchy, tenant model, source-of-record relationships, policy consumption, Tool Gateway boundary, long-term memory strategy, or canonical component placement.

Historical Context Packages shall retain their original schemas and source identities. Migration shall not rewrite the context used for a prior decision.

### Backup, Recovery, and Reconstructibility

Context Engine state may include source catalogs, policies, transformations, caches, manifests, packages, and indexes. Recovery objectives shall distinguish authoritative configuration, reconstructible derived data, and records required for accountability.

Recovery shall verify:

- current identity, tenant, policy, revocation, and access state;
- source availability and versions;
- Immutable Context compatibility;
- schema, ranking, transformation, and cache versions;
- data deletion, retention, and legal-hold state;
- provider eligibility;
- Audit Engine and Evidence Chain reconciliation;
- prevention of stale or revoked package reuse; and
- validation of restored high-impact context paths.

Restoring a cache or Context Package shall not revive access that has been revoked or data that should have been deleted. Reconstructible data may be rebuilt from approved sources and manifests.

### Governance and Roles

Governance shall assign accountable ownership for:

- context purpose, scope, and product claims;
- Immutable Context integration;
- source registration, authority, and lifecycle;
- tenant, authorization, privacy, classification, and region;
- Retrieval Plans, ranking, transformation, summarization, and caching;
- instruction hierarchy and injection resistance;
- Knowledge Graph and Repository Intelligence integration;
- model and provider eligibility;
- context quality, evaluation, Confidence Assessments, and human review;
- correction, deletion, retention, legal hold, and source exit;
- operations, monitoring, incident, backup, and recovery;
- change, release, rollback, deprecation, and retirement; and
- audit, evidence, records, documentation, customer transparency, and support.

No model, provider, source owner, retrieval framework, ranking method, user preference, customer comment, sales commitment, or engineering convenience may approve its own authority or override canonical controls.

Separation of duties shall be proportionate to impact. The person who adds a high-impact source or changes instruction precedence shall not be the sole claimed independent evaluator, policy integrator, production deployer, exception approver, and incident closer under the Enterprise Profile.

### Single-Maintainer Bootstrap Profile

A registered Single-Maintainer Bootstrap Profile may temporarily combine source, retrieval, transformation, evaluation, and operational roles. The absence of independent review shall be recorded and shall not be represented as Enterprise separation of duties.

The bootstrap profile shall maintain:

- exact Immutable Context, tenant, purpose, source, and package binding;
- explicit self-review and exact change attribution;
- mandatory automated authorization, tenant, schema, provenance, injection, privacy, deletion, cache, and Quality Gates;
- protected Audit Engine and Evidence Chain records;
- restricted sources, data classes, tenants, model routes, context consumers, production influence, and release maturity;
